status.heading: Build status
status.lede: Careers@GFTV is being built and released in phases, in public. This page lists every phase, what it covers, and whether it is live yet. It doubles as the changelog.
status.loadError: The status file could not be loaded. Try reloading the page.
status.summaryAllShipped: Every phase has shipped. This page stays as the changelog.
status.summaryBuilding: {shipped} of {total} phases are live. Phase {number}, {name}, is being built now.
status.datesBody: There are none, and none are promised. A phase ships when it works, not on a date announced in advance. What this page does promise is that nothing is shown as available before it is, and that a feature which has not shipped says so on the control itself rather than quietly failing.
home.readFirstBody: Every posting will be public in full. The description, the responsibilities, the requirements, the commitment, and the closing date. An account is only needed for the act of applying.
home.noQueueBody: Applicant accounts are active immediately. There is no approval wait and no email verification, so registering takes a moment.
home.offlineBody: Offline support is still being built. When it arrives, postings you have opened stay readable with no connection, and Careers@GFTV installs to a home screen like an app.
home.bilingualBody: Every posting is published in both English and Simplified Chinese, and you can switch at any time with the globe in the header. A posting we have not translated yet still appears, marked English only. If a translation reads wrongly, there is a link at the foot of the posting to tell us.

auth.alreadySignedInStaff: You are already signed in as

security.heading: Sign in and security
security.noCodesBanner: You have no account recovery codes left. There is no email on this site, so without a code nobody can get you back into this account on their own. Generate a new set now.
security.recoveryBody: Ten codes, each usable once, that set a new password when you have forgotten yours. Treat one like your password: anybody holding a code can take the account.
security.generateWarning: Generating a new set immediately cancels every code in that set. The other set is untouched.
security.backupBody: A different set of ten, for getting past the second step of signing in when you cannot reach Telegram. They never set a password and they are never accepted on the recovery page.
security.twoFactorBody: A code from the Careers@GFTV Telegram bot at every sign in. The bot itself is a later phase, so the switch is here and turned off rather than missing.
security.twoFactorToggle: Ask for a Telegram code when I sign in
security.passwordConsequences: Changing your password signs out every other browser and removes every trusted device.
security.devicesBody: A trusted device skips the second step of signing in for 30 days. It never skips your password, and it never gets past anything in the danger zone.
security.moreSettings: The rest of your account settings
devices.none: No trusted devices. You will be asked for the second step every time you sign in.
security.passkeyBody: A passkey is your fingerprint, your face, or a security key, used as the second step of signing in. There is no code to type and nothing to copy, and a passkey cannot be phished: your device will only use it on this site.
security.passkeySecondStep: Your password is still asked for every time. Once you add a passkey, signing in becomes two steps.
security.passkeyNone: No passkeys yet. Signing in is one step, your password.
security.passkeySynced: Synced to your account, so it survives a lost device
security.passkeyUnsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys. Try a current version of Chrome, Safari, Edge, or Firefox.
security.passkeyDomainNote: A passkey belongs to the site that created it, so this one works on Careers@GFTV and nowhere else. If you lose the device it is on, a two factor backup code gets you past this step.
security.passkeyFailed: That passkey could not be added. Try again.
security.passkeyNeedsBackupCodes: You have no two factor backup codes. Generate a set now: without one, a lost device means you cannot get past the second step.
security.passkeyLastRemoved: That was your last passkey. Signing in is one step again, your password.

home.unpaidHeading: Every role listed today is unpaid
home.unpaidBody: GFTV is run by volunteers, and every posting on this site right now is voluntary and unpaid. That includes the staff and admin roles. We call this Careers@GFTV because it is where the openings are, not because they come with a salary. If a paid role is ever posted, that posting will say so on itself, and roles are labelled by how much time they take, so a full time posting can still be a full time volunteer one.

staffSecurity.pageTitle: Staff sign in and security | Careers@GFTV
staffSecurity.heading: Sign in and security
staffSecurity.elsewhere: Your password, your authenticator app, and your backup codes belong to your gftv.asia account and are changed there. This page covers only what is specific to Careers@GFTV.
staffSecurity.passkeyScope: A passkey belongs to the site that created it, so one added here works on Careers@GFTV and not at gftv.asia. Your authenticator app still works on both.
staffSecurity.passkeyNoneWithTotp: No passkeys yet. Signing in uses your authenticator app for the second step.
staffSecurity.passkeyNoneNoTotp: No passkeys yet, and no authenticator app either, so signing in is one step. Adding a passkey here is the quickest way to change that.
staffSecurity.lastFactorRemoved: That was your last second factor on this portal. Signing in is one step again, your password.
security.passwordForChanges: Asked for because this changes how signing in works. A session on its own is not enough.

about.heading: About Careers@GFTV
about.lede: Careers@GFTV is where Global Furry Television lists the roles it is looking for people to fill, and where you apply for them.
about.whoBody: Global Furry Television is a furry television channel based in Singapore. We produce studio shows, live broadcasts, and convention coverage, and everything we make is made by volunteers. In Mandarin we are 国际兽视, and this portal is 国际兽视 Careers.
about.unpaidHeading: Every role listed here is unpaid
about.unpaidBody1: This is the most important thing on this page, so it is near the top. Every posting currently on this site is voluntary and unpaid. That includes the senior roles, the staff roles, and the people who built this website. Nobody at GFTV is paid today.
about.unpaidBody2: We call it Careers@GFTV because it is where the openings are, not because the openings come with a salary. Roles are labelled by how much time they take, so a posting can honestly say full time and still be a full time volunteer role.
about.unpaidBody3: If a paid role is ever posted, that posting will say so on itself rather than us quietly changing the wording here. That is a fact stored against each posting, not a sentence somebody remembered to update.
about.applyingBody1: Reading a posting needs no account. The description, the responsibilities, the requirements, the commitment, and the closing date are all public, in full, with nothing blurred out. An account is only needed for the act of applying.
about.applyingBody2: Applications themselves are handled in Google Forms. When you apply, the form opens in a new tab with the details you have already given us filled in. We do not store your answers, and we do not accept file uploads anywhere on this site.
about.languagesBody: The whole site exists in both English and Chinese, including the postings themselves, and you can switch at any time with the globe in the header. Your choice is remembered in your browser. A posting that has not been translated yet is still shown rather than hidden, with a note saying it is in English only, because hiding a real opening from the people the translation exists to serve would be the worse failure.
about.buildHeading: This site is still being built
about.buildBody: Careers@GFTV is being released in phases, in public. Anything that has not been built yet says so plainly on the control itself rather than failing quietly or pretending, and the build status page lists every phase and what it covers.
about.contactBody: The frequently asked questions page covers most of them, including what happens after you apply and how to get back into your account if you lose your password.
faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.lede: The questions we are asked most. If yours is not here, the about page covers what Careers@GFTV is and how it works.
faq.paidA: No. Every role currently listed is voluntary and unpaid, including the senior and staff roles, and including the people who built this site. If a paid role is ever posted, that posting will say so on itself. Never assume a posting is paid because it says full time: that describes how much time it takes, not what it pays.
faq.accountQ: Do I need an account to read a posting?
faq.accountA: No. Every posting is public in full, and so is the whole job board including the filters. An account is only needed for the act of applying, and for saving a role to come back to.
faq.registerQ: How long does registering take, and is there an approval queue?
faq.registerA: A moment, and no. Applicant accounts are active immediately. There is no approval wait and no email verification step, because there is no email involved at all.
faq.emailQ: Why does the site not ask for my email?
faq.emailA: Because we send none. Everything we need to tell you appears in your account on this site, and you can link Telegram later if you would rather be told there as well. One consequence is worth knowing before you sign up rather than after: there is no reset link we can send you, so your recovery codes are how you get back in.
faq.recoveryQ: What happens if I forget my password?
faq.recoveryA: You use one of the ten recovery codes you were given when you registered. Save them somewhere you will still have them if you lose the device you are reading this on. If you have also set up a passkey, resetting your password needs both the code and the passkey, which is deliberate: a single lost code should not be enough to take an account over.
faq.applyA: The application form opens in a new tab, in Google Forms, with the details you have already given us filled in. We do not store your answers or accept file uploads. When you come back to this tab we ask whether you submitted it, because that is the only way we can tell.
faq.experienceQ: I have never done this before. Should I still apply?
faq.experienceA: For anything tagged beginner welcome, yes, and we mean it. Those roles come with someone showing you how, on real shoots. Where a posting genuinely needs experience it says so under requirements rather than leaving you to guess.
faq.remoteQ: Do I have to be in Singapore?
faq.remoteA: It depends on the role, and each posting says. Editing, subtitling, design, and social roles are usually remote. Anything involving a camera, a studio, or a convention is not.
faq.deadlineA: That the posting has no closing date. We review applications as they arrive and close the posting when we have found somebody. A posting with a date shows it, and one closing within a fortnight is marked so on the card.
faq.languageQ: Can I use the site in Chinese?
faq.languageA: Yes. Use the globe in the header. The whole site is bilingual, including the postings, and your choice is remembered in this browser. A posting we have not translated yet still appears, marked English only, rather than being hidden from you.
faq.translationQ: A translation reads wrongly. Can I tell you?
faq.translationA: Yes, and please do. Every posting carries a "Report a translation problem" link at the foot. Tell us which language version reads wrongly, which part, and what is wrong, and offer a better wording if you have one. An admin reads every suggestion before anything changes, so nothing you write goes live on its own. Nobody on our side necessarily reads both languages well enough to catch a bad posting first, so these reports are how they get found.
faq.searchQ: Search in Chinese does not seem to rank as well. Is it broken?
faq.searchA: No, but it does work differently, and it is fairer to say so than to let you wonder. English search understands words and ranks results by how well they match. Chinese search matches on the characters you type, because the database cannot split Chinese into words. Both find what is there; only English orders it by relevance.
faq.buildQ: Parts of the site say they are not built yet. Why?
faq.buildA: Because they are not, and we would rather say so than hide the control and let you conclude the feature does not exist. Careers@GFTV is being released in phases, in public. The build status page lists every phase, what it covers, and whether it is live.

faq.reapplyQ: Can I apply for the same role twice?
faq.reapplyA: Not straight away. Once you have told us you applied, that role is closed to you for three months, and both the posting and the job board show the date it reopens rather than letting you find out by clicking. Closing the question without answering it does not start that period, because we only count an application you have confirmed. A role that closes and is later reposted is a new posting, so it carries no waiting period at all.

settings.deletedForms: Anything you already sent through a Google application form is held by Google, not by us, and is not deleted by this. Ask the team if you need those removed.
admin.heading: Overview
admin.lede: What has happened on the board since you were last here.
admin.maintenanceBanner: {count} features are switched off across the site at the moment.
admin.pipelineLede: Every bucket, with a live count. Opening one goes straight to the tracking page already filtered.
admin.draftsWithoutForm: {count} drafts cannot be published yet, because they have no application form.
admin.colAllPostingsHint: Every posting carrying it, drafts included. This is the number that deleting the tag would affect.
admin.jobsLede: Every posting, in every state. A posting is never deleted to take it down: closing keeps it readable and archiving takes it off the board, and both keep everything attached to it.
admin.noJobs: No postings yet. The first one starts as a draft.
admin.noFormHint: This posting cannot be published until it has an application form.
admin.carriesQuestionsHint: Everybody who applies to this role is asked these.
admin.cannotPublish: That posting is not ready to publish.
admin.blocker_no_tags: It needs at least one tag.
admin.deleteJobIrreversible: This cannot be undone. Archiving keeps everything and takes the role off the board, and is almost always the right answer instead.
admin.deleteImpactAnalytics: {count} rows of view and apply history
admin.deleteImpactTasks: {count} tasks mention it, and they stay without the posting
admin.deleteImpactUnknown: What goes with this posting could not be counted. Do not delete it until it can be.
admin.editorLede: The first tab is the posting itself. Every other tab is that language's translation, and a posting may go out in one language only.
admin.translationReady: This translation is ready for readers to see
admin.translationReadyHint: Until this is ticked the translation sits here unseen. It needs a title, a summary, and a description before it can be ticked.
admin.readyNeeds: needed before this language can go live
admin.markdownHint: A small amount of formatting is understood: paragraphs, bullet points, bold, and links. Nothing else.
admin.sectionsHint: Anything beyond the fixed fields above. Headings are content and translate with everything else.
admin.sectionsTranslationHint: This language may carry a different number of sections from the original. Merging two is not a mistake.
admin.embedAlwaysEnglish: Link previews are always served in English, because the site that unfurls the link has no language preference. A Chinese line here will not appear in Discord or Telegram.
admin.embedFallbackNote: Left empty, so this is the first sentence of the description. That is usually right.
admin.slugHint: An alias only. The real address of a posting is its id, so this can be changed without breaking anything.
admin.commitmentHint: One of the five the board filters by. A posting need not state one.
admin.paidHint: Every role is unpaid unless this is ticked. The card and the posting both say which, as a fact about this role rather than a promise in the site copy.
admin.noDeadlineHint: A posting with no closing date stays open until somebody closes it. Nothing closes it automatically.
admin.formUrlHint: A Google Forms address. A posting cannot be published without one.
admin.sheetUrlHint: The Google Sheet the form writes into. Staff only, and never in anything a reader sees.
admin.prefillHint: Optional, as {"entry.123": "email"}. It only works on a long form viewform address, never on a forms.gle short link, and the applicant can still edit what is filled in.
admin.tagHint: A posting needs at least one tag before it can be published, because tags are how somebody filters the board.
admin.postingQuestions: Questions asked of everybody who applies
admin.postingQuestionsHint: Optional. Anybody who applies from now on is asked these as a separate task. Editing them changes only what the next applicant is asked.
admin.errorOnTab: There is something to fix on the {language} tab.
admin.questionsAtCap: That is the most questions one set can carry, which is {max}.
admin.noQuestions: No questions. The applicant gets the message and a reply box.
admin.questionHelp: Help text, if it needs one
admin.questionRequired: This one has to be answered
admin.questionMissingHint: A language left blank falls back to one that was written, so this is a note rather than a problem.
admin.questionOptionsHint: The value is what the answer stores and is the same in every language. The label beside it is what the applicant reads.
admin.applicationsLede: Who was handed over to which form, and where each one has got to. The answers themselves are in Google Forms: each row links out to its posting's response sheet.
admin.selectAll: Select every row on this page
admin.openTaskHint: There is an open task on this applicant for this role.
admin.answersElsewhere: What they wrote on the form is in Google Sheets, not here. This page tracks the handover and the status.
admin.internalNoteHint: Staff only. The applicant never sees it.
admin.waiveHint: This lets them apply to this role again straight away. Changing the status does not.
admin.cooldownWaived: The waiting period has been waived.
admin.noTasks: Nothing has been asked of this applicant.
admin.acceptExplainer: Accepting closes this role to this applicant for good. It does not close the posting or change how many openings it has: do that yourself when you are ready.
admin.rejectExplainer: They can apply again once their waiting period runs out. This is the message most worth writing properly, so write it as a person rather than as a form.
admin.messageBodyPlaceholder: Write what you would say to them.
admin.messageBodyHint: There is no template on purpose. It lands in their outstanding tasks, and phase 11 will also send it to Telegram for anybody who has linked an account.
admin.messageTitleRequired: Write a subject before sending it.
admin.cooldownUntouched: Neither accepting nor rejecting touches the waiting period. Whatever they were serving, they carry on serving.
admin.taskTypeHint: A request asks for something back. A notice is one way, and can be dismissed once it is read.
admin.questionsHint: Optional, up to twenty. The applicant answers them in one submission, along with anything else they want to write.
admin.frozenWarning: Once this is sent, the questions are fixed. Editing them afterwards would leave answers attached to questions nobody asked, so there is no way to do it.
admin.departmentsLede: A team appears on every job card and in the search filters, so an active one needs a name in every language the site offers.
admin.teamActive: Show this team on the site
admin.teamActiveHint: A team cannot be shown until it has a name in every language.
admin.tagsLede: Tags are how somebody filters the board. Two tags that mean the same thing split a search in half, so merge them rather than leaving both.
admin.noOrphanTags: Every tag is on at least one posting.
admin.tagColourHint: A tag with no colour of its own follows the theme, including into dark mode, which a fixed colour does not.
admin.tagSlugFixed: The web address stays {slug}, so a link somebody has shared keeps working.
admin.mergeExplainer: Every posting carrying {name} gains the tag you choose below, and {name} is then deleted.
admin.mergeWarning: {name} disappears, along with its own translations. It is on {count} postings.
admin.maintenanceLede: Turn a feature that has shipped off temporarily, for an outage or while something is being fixed. It goes back on the same way.
admin.maintenanceRules: An override survives a deploy, because it is a database row rather than a file, and nothing turns itself back on. A feature left off is left off until somebody comes back for it.
admin.maintenanceNotApplications: This is not the applications toggle. That one says we are not taking applications at the moment, which is a choice; a switch here says something is broken. They read completely differently to somebody who has just been turned away.
admin.deniedLede: Signing in, registration, and this page itself. Turning any of them off would remove the way back.
admin.noFlippableFeatures: Nothing has shipped that can be switched off yet.
admin.noPublicNote: No note was written, so applicants see the plain sentence.
feature.maintenance: Temporarily unavailable while we fix something.
featureName.docs_staff_login: Signing in to the docs site
featureWhere.job_search: The board at /search and the home page.
featureWhere.translation_report: The report link at the foot of every posting.
featureWhere.translation_helpers: The translating page in a helper's own account area, and the language audit on it.
featureWhere.apply: The Apply button on a posting.
featureWhere.ratings: The stars in the handoff modal.
featureWhere.apply_prompt: The question asked on the next visit after applying.
featureWhere.saved_jobs: The bookmark on a card and on a posting.
featureWhere.outstanding_tasks: The account page and its count.
featureWhere.account_settings: The account settings page, including the picture.
featureWhere.admin_applications: The tracking page in this dashboard.
featureDenied.applicant_login: Turning sign in off would lock every applicant out with no way back.
featureDenied.applicant_register: Registration is how somebody gets an account in the first place.
featureDenied.staff_login: Turning staff sign in off would lock you out of this page.
featureDenied.forgot_password: The only way back in for somebody who has lost their password.
featureDenied.recovery_codes: Part of getting back into an account.
featureDenied.passkeys: A second factor. Turning it off would lock out anybody who has only that.
featureDenied.trusted_devices: Part of signing in, and turning it off would not stop a sign in anyway.
featureDenied.admin_dashboard: This page lives inside the dashboard.
featureDenied.admin_maintenance: This is that page. Switching it off would remove the way back.
apply.acceptedSentence: You have been accepted for this role.
apply.refused_accepted: You have already been accepted for this role.
tasks.anythingElseLabel: Anything else you want to add
tasks.anythingElseHint: Optional. The questions above are what we asked for.
status.outagesLede: These have shipped and are switched off at the moment while we fix something. They will be back.
admin.previewNeedsSave: Save the posting once before previewing it. A posting has no address until it exists.
admin.previewBlocked: Your browser blocked the new tab. Allow pop-ups for this site, or open the posting from the View posting link.
job.previewBanner: Preview. Nobody else can see this page.
job.previewBannerBody: You are seeing it because you are signed in as staff. It is rendered exactly as a reader would see it once it is published.
featureWhere.language_switcher: The globe button in the header, on every page.
featureWhere.theme_switcher: The palette button in the header, on every page.
account.maintenanceBanner: Some things are temporarily unavailable while we fix them: {features}.
admin.confirmOffBody: It stops working for everybody straight away, including for anything calling the API directly. Nothing turns it back on by itself.
admin.confirmOnBody: It starts working again for everybody straight away, and the note stops being shown.
admin.notePromptHint: Optional, and shown to applicants exactly as you type it. Nobody writes a better sentence in the middle of an outage than the person looking at it.
admin.deleteTeamKeeps: Nothing else is deleted. The postings themselves are untouched.
admin.createTagBody: Nothing matches it, so this adds a new tag to the list for every posting.
admin.settingsLede: The wording readers see on the home page, which roles are featured, how long somebody waits before applying to the same role again, and whether the board is taking applications at all.
admin.settingDefaultHint: Every other language falls back to this one when it is left empty.
admin.portalTitleHint: Shown in the header and used in page titles. Every language falls back to the default one when it is left empty.
admin.heroCopyHint: The heading and the line under it on the home page.
admin.featuredHint: Chosen roles appear first on the home page, in this order. With none chosen the home page shows the latest published roles instead.
admin.featuredNone: No roles are featured, so the home page shows the latest published ones.
admin.featuredFull: That is the most that can be featured at once ({count}).
admin.featuredDropped: {count} featured roles are no longer published, so they have been left out. Save to forget them.
admin.cooldownZeroHint: Zero switches the waiting period off entirely. Dates already stored are ignored rather than cleared, so turning it back on restores them.
admin.cooldownExistingHint: Changing this does not move a waiting period somebody is already serving. It applies to the next person who applies.
admin.applicationsOpenBody: Applying works normally on every published role.
admin.applicationsClosedBody: Every Apply control is disabled and every apply endpoint refuses, on every role.
admin.applicationsDelayHint: A change takes about a minute to reach somebody who already has a posting open. That is normal and does not mean the change failed.
admin.applicationsNotMaintenance: This is a policy choice and reads as one. Something broken is switched off from Maintenance instead, which says so in different words.
admin.confirmCloseTitle: Close applications across the whole board?
admin.confirmCloseBody: Nobody can apply to any role until this is turned back on. Postings stay readable and nothing is deleted.
admin.confirmOpenBody: Applying starts working again on every published role.
admin.closeConsequenceApply: Anybody part way through applying is turned away, including from a tab they already had open.
admin.applicationsNoteHint: Optional, and kept in the audit log rather than shown to applicants.
admin.applicationsNowClosed: Applications are closed across the board.
admin.analyticsLede: How each posting is doing: who opened it, who clicked Apply, and how many of those told us they went through with it.
admin.rateIsFloor: A click counts as applied only when somebody told us so. Nobody is chased for an answer, so the conversion rate is the lowest the truth can be, never an estimate of it.
admin.noClicksYet: Nobody has clicked Apply on this one yet, so there is no rate to show.
admin.checkFormWhy: At least {clicks} people clicked Apply and fewer than {rate}% told us they applied. That usually means a broken or closed application form rather than a badly written posting.
admin.ratingSuppressed: Ratings are only averaged from {minimum} onwards, so one opinion does not read as a verdict.
admin.chartAlt: Daily counts of times opened, apply clicks, and applicants who told us they applied.
admin.chartTimezone: Days run midnight to midnight {timezone}, which is how the times are stored.
admin.chartEmpty: Nothing has happened on this posting in that period.
admin.dailyTable: The {count} days with something on them
admin.invitesLede: A shortlist is private: it marks who you are thinking about and tells them nothing. An invite reaches the person, so it lands in their outstanding tasks with whatever you write.
admin.shortlistHint: Nothing here has been sent. These people do not know they are on this list.
admin.noShortlist: Nobody is shortlisted for this role yet.
admin.noInvites: Nobody has been invited to this role yet.
admin.noInvitableJobs: There is nothing published or closed to invite anybody to yet.
admin.inviteNoteHint: An invite shows this to the applicant exactly as you write it. On a shortlist it is a private note about why they are on the list.
admin.confirmInviteBody: Each of these people gets a message in their outstanding tasks. They will be told, and it cannot be unsent.
admin.confirmWithdrawBody: The record stays and the message they already have is not taken back. What stops is any reminder about it.
admin.adminsLede: Who can open this dashboard. Roles and accounts themselves belong to gftv.asia; what is decided here is whether an account may come in.
admin.adminsReadOnly: Accounts, passwords, and the admin and editor roles are set at gftv.asia and cannot be changed from here. This page writes one thing: whether an account may open this portal.
admin.adminsNoPasswordReset: There is deliberately no button here to reset somebody else's password. A staff member sets their own with a recovery code and their second factor, which changes their gftv.asia password too.
admin.noStaffAccounts: No staff accounts can reach this portal yet.
admin.accessState_granted: Allowed here, whatever the role says
admin.accessState_denied: Refused here, whatever the role says
admin.roleAdminOpens: Opens everything here, and the admin and developer guides
admin.rolePosterOpens: Opens postings and applicants, and the job poster guide
admin.factorUsed_totp: with a code from an app
admin.grantAccessBody: Find a gftv.asia account by username. Accounts are created there, not here, so somebody with no account cannot be added from this page.
admin.noStaffFound: No gftv.asia account matches that username.
admin.reasonRequired: Why, and this one is required
admin.reasonOptional: Why, if it is worth recording
admin.reasonHint: Kept on the record and in the audit log. Not shown to the person.
admin.confirmAccessBody_granted: They will be able to open the dashboard on their next visit, whatever their gftv.asia role says.
admin.confirmAccessBody_denied: They lose the dashboard immediately, including any tab they already have open. Nothing they wrote is affected, and their gftv.asia account is untouched.
admin.confirmAccessBody_default: The override is removed and their gftv.asia role decides again, including if it changes later.
admin.roleWouldAllow: Their role currently lets them in, so this changes nothing today.
admin.roleWouldRefuse: Their role does not let them in, so this takes their access away today.
admin.accessChanged_denied: {name} can no longer open the dashboard.
admin.accessChanged_default: {name} is back to whatever their gftv.asia role allows.
account.passwordRequired: Set a new password before you carry on.
account.passwordRequiredBody: Somebody on the team has asked you to choose a new password for this account. Change it below and everything else works normally again.
admin.applicantsLede: The accounts themselves. Where an application has got to is the tracking page; this is the person behind it, and everything here is admins only.
admin.noApplicationsYet: This account has not applied to anything.
admin.postingGone: A posting that no longer exists
admin.accountActivity: The last {count} things that happened to this account
admin.deactivateHint: Suspending keeps everything and only stops them signing in. It is reversible from this same panel.
admin.confirmDeactivateBody: They cannot sign in until this is undone, including in any tab they already have open. Their applications, saved roles, and history are all kept.
admin.confirmReactivateBody: Everything goes back to how it was. They will need to sign in again.
admin.lockedOutHint: Prefer these to setting a password. Neither of them tells anybody what the password is, so the record can still say the account holder chose it themselves.
admin.confirmForceReset: Require {name} to set a new password?
admin.confirmForceResetBody: They will be asked to choose one the next time they sign in, and cannot use the account area until they do.
admin.consequenceSessions: Every session and trusted device is ended, so they sign in again everywhere.
admin.consequenceNoPassword: Nobody learns their password, so the record still shows they chose it.
admin.resetForced: {name} will be asked for a new password at their next sign in.
admin.confirmUnlink: Unlink the Telegram account linked to {name}?
admin.confirmUnlinkBody: Only do this after checking who you are speaking to some other way. It is how somebody gets back in when they have lost the account they were signing in with.
admin.setPasswordCost: Setting somebody's password is the one action here that cannot be taken back in the record. Once you know their password, this log can no longer show that they did something themselves rather than you.
admin.setPasswordPrefer: Requiring a new password does the same job without that cost. Use this only when that will not work.
admin.newPasswordHint: Generated here, sixteen characters, and hidden because this screen may be looked at by somebody else. Copy it and pass it on: it cannot be shown again once this is saved. They will be asked to replace it the moment they sign in, and every session and trusted device ends now.
admin.passwordSet: The password for {name} has been set. Pass it on now, because it cannot be shown again.
admin.reasonMissing: A reason is required for this one.
admin.deleteConsequenceRows: Their applications, saved roles, tasks, ratings, passkeys, and codes all go with the account.
admin.deleteConsequenceAnalytics: The funnel numbers and any translation reports stay, with no name attached to them.
admin.deleteConsequenceForms: Anything they submitted through a Google Form is not ours to delete and stays where it is.
admin.deleteConsequenceIrreversible: This cannot be undone. Suspending sign in keeps everything and is almost always the right answer instead.
admin.accountDeleted: The account for {name} has been deleted.
audit.password_reset: Reset their password with a recovery code
audit.applicant_reset_forced: Was required to set a new password
admin.viewsIndicative: Opens are counted once per posting per browsing session and are not unique people. Read them as a rough measure of interest rather than as a headcount.
admin.passwordCopied: Copied. Pass it on now, because it cannot be shown again.
admin.passwordCopyFailed: That could not be copied, so it is shown instead. Take it down before closing this.
admin.translationsLede: What readers have told us reads wrongly, from the form at the foot of a posting and from helpers selecting the words in place, and what nobody has translated yet.
admin.translationsInterfaceNote: Wording in the interface itself, the navigation and the buttons, lives in the code rather than the database. A report about one of those shows its key and is fixed by editing assets/i18n and deploying.
admin.noReports: Nothing in the queue. Every report has been answered.
admin.anchorDetached: These words are no longer in the text this points at, so it cannot be shown in place. The wording has probably been changed since. The suggestion is still worth reading.
admin.noSuggestion: They did not suggest a wording, only said what was wrong.
admin.suggestionNeverApplied: Nothing here is applied on its own. Whatever is in the box below is what gets saved.
admin.interfaceIsCode: This wording is in the code, in assets/i18n, which is what lets the site work offline. Fixing it means editing that file and deploying. There is no editor for it here, deliberately.
admin.noTranslationRow: This language has no translation of this yet, so readers are seeing the original. Saving below starts one, and it stays unpublished until somebody marks the language ready in the editor.
admin.notEditableHere: This one cannot be rewritten from here. Either they did not say which part reads wrongly, or it is a part that has to be edited with everything around it.
admin.wordingHint: This saves the wording and nothing else. It does not close the report, and it does not make an unpublished translation live.
admin.wordingSaved: The wording is saved. Say what happened before closing the report.
admin.resolutionNoteHint: The person who raised this reads exactly what you write here, on their own account page. Required to mark it fixed or not a problem, including when they were mistaken.
admin.resolutionNeedsNote: Say what happened. Whoever raised this reads it.
admin.statusHint_open: Waiting for somebody. This is where a report arrives.
admin.statusHint_accepted: Somebody has picked this up. It comes off the sidebar count and stays in the queue.
admin.statusHint_fixed: The wording has been changed. Needs a note.
admin.statusHint_rejected: The wording is right as it stands. Needs a note saying why, because they took the trouble to tell us.
admin.noFieldNamed: They did not say which part reads wrongly, so there is nothing single to show here. Open it in the editor and read their note beside it.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceRows: {count} tracking rows go, and with them the record that these people were handed over to a form at all.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceEvents: {count} status changes go with them, so how each one got to where it is cannot be looked up again.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceCooldown: {count} of them are serving a reapply cooldown, and it ends now. Those people can apply to the same role again immediately.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceTasks: {count} tasks stay with the applicant and stop pointing at anything.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceAnalytics: The funnel numbers on the analytics page are not affected. They are a separate record and survive this.
admin.deleteRowsConsequenceApplicant: It disappears from the applicant’s own list of applications, and they are not told.
admin.deleteRowsIrreversible: This cannot be undone. Moving a row to Withdrawn takes it out of the working list and keeps everything, and is almost always the right answer instead.
admin.auditNote: What nobody has translated yet, whether or not anybody has complained. Three states: nothing in this language at all, drafted but not marked ready, and live but thinner than the original. A translation that is finished is not on this list.
admin.auditFinished: Nothing is left to translate into {language}. Every posting, team, and tag has one, and none of them is thinner than the original.
admin.auditNeedsSecondLanguage: This site has one language, so there is nothing to audit. Adding a second one to gftvjobs_locales is what fills this in.
admin.searchApplicantHint: Name, username, or email address. It searches every page, not only the rows on screen.
admin.searchTruncated: More than 200 people match that. Only the first 200 are listed here, and an export with this filter carries the same 200. Add a role or a date range to narrow it.
admin.helpersNote: A helper is an ordinary applicant account granted the right to edit translations in one language. They draft freely and cannot make anything live: only an admin sets a translation ready, so access can be granted before trust is.
admin.grantHelperBody: Choose the language first, then find the account. A helper edits every translation in that language, on every posting, and cannot make any of them live.
admin.noHelpers: Nobody holds the helper role yet. Granting it is how somebody who reads the language starts fixing it.
admin.confirmGrantHelperBody: They will be able to edit every {language} translation on the site, on any posting, team, or tag.
admin.helperCannotPublish: They cannot make a translation live. Only an admin marks one ready, so nothing they write reaches a reader until you say so.
admin.helperEditsEverything: It is the whole language, not one posting. There is no way to grant {language} for part of the site.
admin.helperReasonHint: Recorded on the row and read off this list a year from now. Say who they are and who vouched for them.
admin.helperReasonNeeded: Say why before granting or revoking. This one is required.
admin.confirmRevokeHelperBody: They keep their account and lose the helper area for {language}.
admin.revokeKeepsTranslations: Everything they have already written stays exactly as it is, live or not.
admin.revokeIsLoggedOnly: The row is deleted, so this reason and the audit log are the only record that they ever held it.
admin.revokeReasonHint: Kept in the audit log. There is no revoked row to read it off later.
helper.heading: Translating
helper.lede: What is still waiting to be written in your language, and the place to write it. Nothing you save here goes live on its own.
helper.gateBody: This area is for translation helpers. The role is granted for one language at a time by an admin, and it lets you write and improve that language across the whole site.
helper.gateAsk: Anyone can report a translation that reads wrongly from the link at the foot of any posting. That needs no role at all.
helper.whatSavingDoes: You can write and rewrite this language freely, with no approval and no waiting. A posting stays a draft until an admin marks it ready, so nothing you write there reaches readers until somebody has read it. A team or tag name has no draft state and changes as soon as you save it.
helper.findHint: Search by the name it has in English. A translation that is already finished is not on the list below, so this is how to go back and improve one.
helper.nothingMissing: Nothing missing. It is waiting to be marked ready.
helper.nothingInSource: The original leaves this empty, so there is nothing to translate here.
helper.draftUntilReady: This translation is not live yet. Save as often as you like: an admin marks it ready once it is finished, and only then do readers see it.
helper.alreadyLive: This translation is live. What you save changes what readers see now, so it cannot be left without a title, a summary, and a description.
helper.liveAtOnce: This one has no draft state. A team or tag name appears wherever it is used as soon as you save it.
helper.tooManySections: A translation may carry at most {count} extra sections.
helper.discardBody: What you have typed here has not been saved, and leaving will lose it.
helper.savedNew: Saved. This language now has its own version of this.
helper.switchedOff: Helping with translations has been switched off for the moment. Your role is unchanged and the area comes back when it does.
